title: a review is not thrown away because main moved during the round: the final check before recording a verdict requires the same PR head and the same base branch name, not an unchanged base tip, and gate 7 alone decides whether the verdict covers a later head
acceptance: Why. A review round that finishes after main has moved is thrown away. On 2026-10-04/05 the reviews of T-190, T-192 and T-195 were each discarded this way and rerun in full when another PR merged during the round. Example: reviewer-nils-t192-r1b's REJECT went to stale-final.txt at 17:05:55Z, 22 s after #179 merged at 17:05:33Z; the PR head itself did not move until the autopilot's branch update at 17:07:01Z. The discard is decided by the final call `if ! verify_review_head; then ... stale-final.txt ... exit 65` at bin/fm-review.sh:1247-1253. verify_review_head (bin/fm-review.sh:288-304) fails on a base move in three places: (1) `fm_binding head` (:297) -> fm_binding.py authoritative() (:113-127) calls verified_base() (:244-254), which raises 'local base is stale; synchronize before accepting' whenever the live base tip differs from the local base ref, and then refuses if baseRefOid changed between its two reads (:124-126); (2) `fm_binding base` (:301) -> view_base() -> the same verified_base() freshness check; (3) the explicit tip comparison `git rev-parse "$REVIEW_PR_BASE^{commit}" = "$REVIEW_PR_BASE_HEAD"` (:302). None of these protects the verdict: the reviewed source is bound by R_HEAD, R_BASE (merge-base) and R_PATCH (`git patch-id --stable`) computed at :376-378 from the head, not from main's tip, and gate 7 (`fm_evidence gate`, bin/lib/fm_evidence.py:356-383, called from gate7() at bin/fm-gate.sh:251-265) already decides whether a verdict for an older head covers the current head (same patch-id, reviewed base an ancestor of the current merge-base, unchanged spec/contract/conventions hashes).

Final check. verify_review_head keeps its name and its current behaviour when called with no argument (the calls at bin/fm-review.sh:305 and :813, and tests/external-execution.test.sh:229-245, which extracts the function by name and expects a moved or unreadable head to fail and a matching head to pass). It gains one optional argument: `verify_review_head final`, used only at :1247. In final mode it (a) returns 0 for a local-only review with no PR, as today; (b) reads the PR once through a new read-only binding mode (below) and requires: the PR is open, its headRefOid equals R_HEAD, the fetched refs/pull/<n>/head equals R_HEAD, the local task ref equals R_HEAD, and its baseRefName equals REVIEW_PR_BASE (a PR retargeted to another base during the round is still stale); (c) does NOT require the local base ref to equal the live base tip and does NOT compare REVIEW_PR_BASE_HEAD. A moved head, a retargeted base, a closed or merged PR, or any read failure keeps today's stale path unchanged (stale-final.txt, review_failed with --review-outcome infrastructure_error, exit 65). The verdict is always recorded with the R_HEAD/R_BASE/R_PATCH computed at the start of the round (:1255-1258 unchanged); nothing is re-bound to a newer head.

Binding mode. bin/lib/fm_binding.py gains a mode `review-final` (add it to the `choices` list at :284) taking --task, --pr, --branch and --head <reviewed sha> and a new --base-name <expected base name>. It calls remote_head() once (which already refuses a PR that is not OPEN and validates both OIDs), validates baseRefName as verified_base() does (non-empty, no leading '-') but performs no live-tip fetch and no local-base comparison, requires baseRefName == --base-name, requires headRefOid == --head, fetches refs/pull/<pr>/head with fetch_ref() and requires it == --head, requires `git rev-parse <branch>^{commit}` == --head, and prints the head. Any mismatch raises ValueError with a message naming which of head, fetched head, local task ref or base name differed; it reaches stderr through fm_binding.py's existing `fm-binding: <reason>` line (bin/lib/fm_binding.py:363-368), which verify_review_head does not suppress. No new stderr line is added in fm-review.sh; the stale path keeps its existing review_failed event text. Review-verdict case (2) asserts that stderr contains `fm-binding:` and the word base. The existing modes (base, head, checks, ready, candidate, external-review, local-gate-base) are unchanged; in particular gates, readiness and merge candidates keep requiring a fresh local base. fm_binding in bin/fm-config.sh:1133-1140 needs no change (it passes all arguments through).

One carry rule. fm-review.sh adds no carry or coverage logic of its own. Whether a recorded verdict covers a later head stays decided only by `fm_evidence gate` (bin/lib/fm_evidence.py:369-383) through gate 7. This task does not change that rule. Accepted risk, stated in the design text: a semantic conflict introduced by main outside the reviewed files (for example main renames a function the PR calls) is not seen by the reviewer; it is caught only by the required CI on the current head (gate 6), exactly as for today's gate 7 carry across a merge of main.

Autopilot interaction (checked, no change). After a base move the autopilot's branch update (fm_autopilot_branches.py) produces a new head whose patch-id normally equals R_PATCH, so gate 7 accepts the recorded verdict and the autopilot proceeds to a merge card; it launches a review only when the gate exits 7 (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:322-330, launch_review :303-307). The review-job completion check (:335-339) compares the verdict's head with the PR head captured at launch, which is R_HEAD in the newly accepted case, so it raises no attention. The autopilot already holds branch updates while a reviewer round is live (round_live in fm_autopilot_branches.py), so in normal operation the head does not move under a review. No change to bin/lib/fm_autopilot*.py (T-200 and the ledger-removal tasks own those files).

Tests: binding mode. Extend tests/live-base-binding.test.sh. Its gh stub answers `pr view --json headRefOid,baseRefOid,baseRefName,headRefName,state` in GitHub's real shape but hard-codes state OPEN and headRefOid 'c'*40 (:35-37); its fetch stub serves values from PR_HEAD and LIVE_BASE (FETCH_FILE is only storage, :51-60); and `rev-parse task^{commit}` returns PR_HEAD (:63-64). Extend the stubs with separate controls (for example PR_STATE, VIEW_HEAD, FETCHED_PULL_HEAD, LOCAL_TASK_HEAD, VIEW_BASE_NAME), defaulting to today's values so existing cases are unchanged. New cases for `review-final`: live base tip differs from the local base ref and baseRefOid differs, head and base name match -> exit 0 and prints the head (with the same setup assert `base` and `head` modes fail, so the test proves the difference); baseRefName differs from --base-name -> nonzero, stderr names the base; view head differs -> nonzero; fetched pull head differs -> nonzero; local task ref differs -> nonzero; state CLOSED and MERGED -> nonzero. Fail-first: each new case is red before the mode exists (argparse rejects 'review-final').

Tests: review round end to end. Add cases to tests/review-verdict.test.sh using its fixture (tests/lib/review.sh fixture/ghstub) and a mock adapter that, while 'reviewing', performs the move under test before writing its verdict; extend the gh stub only as needed so `pr view` answers in GitHub's real JSON shape (headRefOid, baseRefOid, baseRefName, headRefName, state) and refs are served from the fixture repo, never from what the code expects. Cases: (1) an unrelated commit lands on the base branch (main) during the round, PR head unchanged -> exit 0, the verdict is recorded (`fm_evidence` verdict exists with head == the reviewed head), the verdict is projected, approved/review_failed is emitted as for a normal round, and no stale-final.txt exists; this case is red on main today. (2) The PR is retargeted to another base during the round (the mock adapter writes $FM_TARGET_ROOT/.fixture-pr-base) -> exit 65, stale-final.txt exists, review_failed with outcome infrastructure_error, no verdict recorded. (3) The PR head moves during the round -> exit 65 and stale, as today (regression). (4) The PR is closed during the round (.fixture-pr-closed) -> stale (regression). Existing assertions in the suites listed in the fixtures item and in board-wake.test.sh, crew-end-to-end.test.sh, external-execution.test.sh and role-prompts.test.sh that mention stale or moved heads keep passing unchanged; if one pins the old base-tip behaviour, change it and say why in the PR.

Test fixtures that imitate fm_binding.py. (a) tests/lib/binding-fixture.sh binding_service_fixture (:5-37), installed by tests/lib/review.sh:67 (stack_base_fixture follows at :68) into every review fixture, replaces bin/lib/fm_binding.py and keeps its own copy of the handled modes list (:18: head, base, checks, ready, candidate; anything else runs the real implementation, which in these fixtures has no origin, no GH_REPO and a gh stub that prints nothing, so a real `review-final` would always fail and every `fm-review.sh --pr` round in a fixture would end stale with exit 65). Add `review-final` to that list and answer it like the fixture's `head` mode: parse --head and --base-name; the head is `git -C $FM_TARGET_ROOT rev-parse <branch>`; fail (exit 1, message on stderr) if it differs from --head; the PR's base name is the content of `$FM_TARGET_ROOT/.fixture-pr-base` when that file exists, else FM_BASE, else 'main', and the fixture's `base` mode reads the same source (in review.sh fixtures stack_base_fixture answers `base` itself with 'main', so there the retarget case works because `review-final` reads the file and compares it with REVIEW_PR_BASE=main); fail if it differs from --base-name; fail if `$FM_TARGET_ROOT/.fixture-pr-closed` exists. (b) tests/lib/stack-base-fixture.sh stack_base_fixture (:4-15) answers only `base` and forwards every other mode to the prior fm_binding.py, so `review-final` reaches binding_service_fixture where that is the prior; no change needed beyond confirming each suite below. (c) tests/lib/head-binding.sh head_binding_fixture (:4-26) gives the real binding local git transport and GitHub-shaped `pr view` replies (:16); used by tests/stacking-binding.test.sh:15 (review round at :36 with the PR base `work`), gate.test.sh and gate-project-base.test.sh; it already answers in the shape `review-final` reads, so it should need no change; confirm. (d) tests/lib/run_project_turns.py:54 replaces fm_binding with `echo fixture-head` for every mode; verify_review_head final compares the printed head with R_HEAD exactly as head mode does, so that stub keeps its current meaning; no change. Suites that run `fm-review.sh --pr` through these fixtures and must stay green unchanged: tests/review-verdict.test.sh, review-checkout.test.sh, review-diff.test.sh, review-retry.test.sh, review-evidence.test.sh, gate.test.sh, local-round-loop.test.sh, e2e-loop.test.sh, stacking-binding.test.sh (real binding through head_binding_fixture), and tests/codex-review-integration.test.sh, which runs the real bin/fm-review.sh --pr 9 (:156-157) with the real fm_binding.py and a real-shape gh stub (:95-98), moves `work` during the CI wait (:88-89; that move must still be caught by the unchanged check at bin/fm-review.sh:813, not by the final check) and asserts the recorded verdict's head, base and patch (:212-214); it is expected to pass unchanged. The PR lists each of these suites and says whether it needed a change.

Docs. design/design.md §15.7 'Portable roles and stock execution', the paragraph at about lines 5088-5092 ('External review requires a PR and compares its authoritative head/base with local refs before preparation, after the CI wait and before publishing the final verdict. A moved or unreadable head retains the final answer as stale evidence ...'), is amended in place: before preparation and after the CI wait the head and a fresh base are required; before recording the verdict the head must be unchanged and the base branch name unchanged, but main having moved does not void the round; the verdict stays bound to the reviewed head and gate 7's existing patch-id rule decides whether it covers a later head; plus the accepted-risk sentence from the 'One carry rule' item. No new section and nothing appended at the end of design.md. docs/ has no text about this check (grep for 'stale' in docs/*.md shows none); none is added.

Callers and mirrors (grep results on 7c9877e). verify_review_head: bin/fm-review.sh:288 (definition), :305, :813, :1247; extracted by name in tests/external-execution.test.sh:229-245 and tests/lib/role_prompts.py:89-96, 146-157, 166-176 (run by tests/role-prompts.test.sh); all of these call it with no argument and keep passing unchanged. stale-final.txt: written only at bin/fm-review.sh:1248; not read elsewhere in bin/, board/, games/ or docs/. fm_binding modes list: bin/lib/fm_binding.py:284, mirrored in tests/lib/binding-fixture.sh:18 (see the fixtures item); tests/lib/stack-base-fixture.sh, tests/lib/head-binding.sh and tests/lib/run_project_turns.py:54 also stand in for fm_binding or GitHub. In bin/lib/fm_binding.py main(), `review-final` must branch off before the shared `head = sha(args.head)` / evidence-store path that starts at :300. Callers of `fm_binding base`/`head` (bin/fm-review.sh, bin/fm-gate.sh, bin/fm-worker.sh, bin/lib/fm_autopilot*.py) are not changed. Snapshots under state/snapshots/ are generated copies and are not edited.

In flight. Rounds already running when this merges keep their frozen code snapshot and behave as today. Verdicts already retained as stale-final.txt stay stale; they are not promoted. Nothing in state/ is migrated. Open PRs need no action. Gate 7, readiness and merge-card rules are unchanged, so no existing approval changes meaning.

Workers do not run tests; the required GitHub check and the gates are the evidence. Scope: bin/fm-review.sh, bin/lib/fm_binding.py, tests/** (the suites named above and tests/lib/review.sh), design/design.md (§15.7 paragraph only), design/tasks/T-201.json. Ordering: T-201 touches no file of T-196 (CI workflow, bin/ci.sh), T-197 (cursor), T-198 (fm-session, fm_host, fm-herdr), T-199 (fm-worker) or the autopilot tasks; it may run in parallel with them, but merges after T-196 so its CI covers every suite.
